key_insight: For long horizons, exploratory stochastic LQ optimal states and control distributions exhibit turnpike behavior around stochastic and distributional reference objects, even with indefinite costs.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a theoretical basis for reference-based approximations in long-horizon control that balances exploration and exploitation.
method: Derive a finite-horizon feedback representation for exploratory stochastic LQ control.
Formulate a static distribution optimization problem to identify the reference object.
Use joint coercivity to prove state-process and Wasserstein control-distribution turnpike properties under stabilizability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mathematical turnpike proofs as the horizon tends to infinity, but describes no datasets or numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Application requires verifying the joint coercivity and stabilizability assumptions; the abstract does not establish practical approximation accuracy at a chosen finite horizon.
paper_title: Turnpike Properties for Exploratory Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Indefinite Cost Functionals
